body: In the revised version of 9.4 the anti-caching header focus has been narrowed down to focus on just browsers. However proxies also play a role here. Many companies terminate SSL in load balancers (which also have proxying functionality), and may accidentally end up serving data cached for one user to another. Also "sufficient anti-caching headers" is a lot weaker than having actual examples in there.
